correctness.rationale: Directed cycles in K_{2,q} require both mixed leaf states; each remaining orientation corresponds to exactly one zonotope vertex. The explicit half-signed-degree vector yields the stated exponent. Branch overlap counting is exact; the completed-square identity, lattice admissibility, strict convexity, parity and binomial expectation formulas hold for all q>=2. Exponentially small binary-overlap mass and a binomial CLT with delta method prove the limits. Independent enumeration of 19166 vertices through q=8 and integer formula checks through q=150 corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The closest structural papers establish a graphical-zonotope face/vertex correspondence and complete-bipartite face counts, while known completed multipartite Euclidean claims cover only outer radius or different measures. The new all-shell multinomial vertex-radius polynomial, inner contact multiplicities, and Gaussian counting-measure radial law are not implied by those claims. Earlier equivalent indegree-imbalance formulas remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Historical equivalence under indegree-imbalance distribution or orientation-majorization terminology has not been ruled out exhaustively.

value.rationale: The complete uniform-vertex radial shell distribution, exact inner-contact multiplicities, parity law and asymptotic Gaussian radius fluctuations together determine a natural Euclidean invariant for all K_{2,q} zonotopes. Distinct from volume covariance, vertex flip degrees and previously known outer circumsphere, the two-sector-to-one-radial-normal phenomenon supplies a structural geometric explanation.
